source_quality.reason: Source episode passed its own tests (11 checks) and submitted a coherent solution. Its limits are that the source implements source-specific task_func(goals, penalties), not the target's league-wide simulate_league(num_matches) contract.

memory_fidelity.reason: Source provenance is retained and observable, but not injected into the target; no target-context source text can be compared with the source episode, so fidelity is unassessable.

target_applicability.reason: Source shares football/random/DataFrame/LinearRegression elements, but the target changes the interface and requires aggregating multiple matches with two teams per match, so only part of the source pattern applies.

visible_use.reason: Target submission implements its own per-match two-team accumulation and never calls source task_func or reuses source example values; visible behavior shows no source-memory reuse.

labels.reason: Source provenance was in observable retrieval candidates but absent from injected_ids; oldest complete episodes were dropped by byte budget. This is packing/visibility loss, not retrieval failure, and does not prove source content was necessary.
A legal, passing source episode exists in history for a closely related task. Its presence alone does not show it was available to or affected the target.

Reference solution aggregates repeated task_func outputs, while submitted target directly increments two randomly chosen teams per match; hidden evaluation still passes with 8 checks, suggesting value-level semantics may not be enforced. This is a candidate contract looseness only.
Six unrelated episodes (~42KB) were injected while the target solved the task with one PYTHON call. This describes observed overhead only; it cannot show harm or absence of benefit.

competing_explanations: Target success may be entirely due to the provided starter code and model coding ability, not memory.
The relevant source may never have been intended as usable memory for this modified contract.
Hidden checks appear structural; different simulation semantics may be accepted without indicating memory transfer.
uncertainties: Whether the source episode was among the dropped oldest episodes cannot be mapped from the supplied IDs alone.
Whether any source content was available to the target agent through an unshown channel.
Whether the target implementation would satisfy exact aggregation semantics if hidden tests compared values.
Whether the six injected unrelated episodes had any behavioral effect.
Token counts are unavailable; only byte counts and partial usage are given.

minimal_intervention.change: Preserve the relevant source episode/provenance in the injected context instead of dropping it by byte budget, while keeping the same target prompt and budget otherwise.
minimal_intervention.fixed: Same source history, target task, memory policy, packing budget, and evaluation checks.
minimal_intervention.falsifier: If injecting the source episode leaves target behavior and evaluation unchanged, or if source content was already in context, the packing-visibility explanation is not supported.
